Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

playback of sandbox media: `SandboxAudioPlayer` (play/pause, seek slider,
  `m:ss / m:ss`) and `SandboxVideoPlayer` (bounded tap-to-toggle surface,
  progress bar, mute) behind injectable `SandboxAudioController`/
  `SandboxVideoController` abstractions (tests/goldens inject fakes via
  `ChatScreen(audioControllerFactory:/videoControllerFactory:)`, real
  defaults wrap `audioplayers` (`BytesSource` — no file needed) and
  `video_player` (bytes staged to a temp file; web build shows an honest
  "not supported" note). Wired in `chat_screen.dart` for `speak`/
  `generate_music` results plus a `.mp3/.wav/.m4a` (audio) / `.mp4/.mov/
  .webm` (video) extension fallback for any NON-`read`, non-error tool
  result (which is how `generate_video` tiles render); markdown media links open a `showFahMediaDialog` player dialog
  (`onTapLink` — flutter_markdown has no custom link renderer) in the chat
  screen and the Fa chat overlay. Bytes load through the same memoized
  `SandboxImageResolver.load`.
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/chat_message_tile.dart` (shim re-export of
  `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/chat_message_tile.dart`) — the ONE transcript
  message renderer, shared by the chat screen (its `flutter_chat_ui`
  builders delegate) and the in-app Fa chat overlay (`compact: true` for
  tighter panel padding): user/assistant Markdown bubbles (sandbox images
  via `SandboxImageResolver`, selectable), tail-collapsed thinking bubble,
  styled `[ tool ]` tiles with the private collapsible output block,
  `$`-prompt system lines, and inline generated-image/audio/video under
  tool tiles. Never fork message rendering — extend this widget.
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/chat_composer.dart` (ADAPTER over
  `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/chat_composer.dart`) — keeps the app's
  constructor surface (`AgentService` + injectable `uploadPicker`/`asr`/
  `asrTranscriber`/`clipboardImageReader` test fakes) and bridges it to the
  shared composer's hooks: the `UploadPicker` becomes a `FaChatUploadPicker`,
  gallery/camera come from `image_picker`, the ASR stack is wrapped in a
  `FaChatVoiceInput` (transcriber resolved per take via the session's
  media gateway, falling back to the active provider), and the smart-paste
  clipboard image probe rides `pasteboard` (`Pasteboard.image` → PNG bytes;
  native plugin — the desktop/mobile apps need a REBUILD, not a hot reload,
  to register it).
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/app_launcher_screen.dart` — THE app home on
  every layout (`faHomeScreen` in main.dart always returns it; the classic
  sidebar chat home is legacy and `session_sidebar.dart` no longer exists —
  sessions are managed by the chat sheet's pager/menus).
  iOS-home-screen grid of the JS apps (fsRevision-refreshed like

## PR Description

## Проблема

Web sign-in из диалога «Sign in with your ai-native.cloud account» был сломан в двух местах:

1. **`Attempting to use a null window in Window.open`** — `NetworkAuthFlow` ждёт сетевой `/initiate` между кликом и `window.open`; к моменту открытия попап теряет transient activation кнопки, браузер блокирует его, а null-backed `WindowBase` падает на любом обращении (в т.ч. на проверке `closed`).
2. **`/oauth/callback` отдавал 404 на GitHub Pages** — статическая receiver-страница из #1048 была удалена коммитом 80a5ebeeb (прямой пуш в main без PR).

## Фикс

- `WebOAuthReceiver.bind()` открывает попап **синхронно в момент клика** (`about:blank`, пока gesture activation жив); `openAuthUrlImpl` лишь навигирует уже открытое окно — навигация существующего окна не требует активации, поэтому `/initiate` RTT между кликом и навигацией безопасен.
- Null-safe `_isUsable` проба (null-backed WindowBase бросает на любом члене), `close()` убирает брошенный попап при провале flow, fallback на прямой open если eager-попап был заблокирован при bind.
- `site/oauth/callback/index.html` восстановлен без изменений (#1048).

Проверено: flutter_app/test/network/* (300 зелёные), auth_flow_test (5 зелёные), анализ чистый. Связано: auth-allowlist fa1.dev — IstiN/learn.ai#69 (уже в проде).

Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. - **Title**: fix(web): restore /oauth/callback page + eager OAuth popup (web sign-in end-to-end)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `fix/web-oauth-popup` → `main`
- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +151
- **Deletions**: -22
- **Created**: 2026-09-29T08:56:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T04:51:56Z

## PR Description

## Проблема

Web sign-in из диалога «Sign in with your ai-native.cloud account» был сломан в двух местах:

1. **`Attempting to use a null window in Window.open`** — `NetworkAuthFlow` ждёт сетевой `/initiate` между кликом и `window.open`; к моменту открытия попап теряет transient activation кнопки, браузер блокирует его, а null-backed `WindowBase` падает на любом обращении (в т.ч. на проверке `closed`).
2. **`/oauth/callback` отдавал 404 на GitHub Pages** — статическая receiver-страница из #1048 была удалена коммитом 80a5ebeeb (прямой пуш в main без PR).

## Фикс

- `WebOAuthReceiver.bind()` открывает попап **синхронно в момент клика** (`about:blank`, пока gesture activation жив); `openAuthUrlImpl` лишь навигирует уже открытое окно — навигация существующего окна не требует активации, поэтому `/initiate` RTT между кликом и навигацией безопасен.
- Null-safe `_isUsable` проба (null-backed WindowBase бросает на любом члене), `close()` убирает брошенный попап при провале flow, fallback на прямой open если eager-попап был заблокирован при bind.
- `site/oauth/callback/index.html` восстановлен без изменений (#1048).

Проверено: flutter_app/test/network/* (300 зелёные), auth_flow_test (5 зелёные), анализ чистый. Связано: auth-allowlist fa1.dev — IstiN/learn.ai#69 (уже в проде).

The dialog serializes providers through one busy slot (per doc comment), and signInWithProvider is invoked from that dialog only... plus tests. The overlap is a real but guarded path. The name-collision navigation behavior is pre-existing (old code also used 'fa_oauth'). The PR makes the blank popup linger longer. I'd rate SUGGESTION with clear reasoning, or IMPORTANT? "When in doubt, start one level higher." The failure mode: two rapid sign-in attempts → confusing failure. It requires UI to allow concurrent sign-in which it doesn't. SUGGESTION.

Actually wait — there's a subtler variant that does NOT require overlapping flows: bind A → user cancels/fails before openAuthUrl (initiate network error) → close() closes popup, `_popup = null`, `_active` cleared. OK that's clean now.

3. **SUGGESTION — Blank popup UX + honest error wording**: If the user closes the eager `about:blank` window during the `/initiate` wait (a featureless blank window invites that), `openAuthUrlImpl` falls to the direct-open fallback, which post-await is usually blocked → the user sees "the sign-in popup was blocked by the browser" though they closed it themselves. Minor wording confusion; the poll that would report "the sign-in window was closed" only starts at trackPopup. Could start the poll at bind or check in fallback. SUGGESTION.

4. **SUGGESTION — `openAuthUrlImpl` control flow is convoluted**: the `receiver?._popup = null` in the catch + re-check dance reads hard; a small local `navigated` bool or early return structure would be clearer. Also `receiver?._popup` null-aware cascade repeated. Style.

5. **SUGGESTION — `_isUsable`'s `closed ?? true` vs old `?? false` semantics**: for a real window `closed` is never null; but if `closed` were somehow indeterminate the new code treats the popup as dead and errors "window was closed". Fine — intentional per doc. Not a finding, skip.

6. **Observation on `trackPopup` poll timer leak if called twice** — pre-existing structure; openAuthUrlImpl can now be re-entered? Only called once per signIn. Skip.

7. **Security**: 
   - Callback page uses `textContent` — no XSS. Good.
   - Popup is `about:blank` (opener-origin) until navigated — the popup has `window.opener` and the app has a handle to the popup; provider pages get `window.opener` reference to our app window... this was true before too (window.open always gives the opened page an opener unless `noopener`). The features string doesn't include `noopener` (and it MUST NOT — the app needs the handle to poll). Pre-existing; the OAuth popup pattern requires it. Not a finding.
   - No secrets logged. The PR stores none.
   - `site/oauth/callback/index.html` — static; could be abused for open-redirect? No — it doesn't redirect anywhere; it just displays status. Fine.

8. **Ticket scope**: matches — restore the callback page (byte-identical), eager popup, null-safety, cleanup. No scope creep.

9. **Backward compat**: internal-only (`WebOAuthReceiver` is private to lib/web impl of the conditional import). `bind()` still returns Future<WebOAuthReceiver>. `trackPopup` signature unchanged. `openAuthUrlImpl` unchanged signature. Good.

10. **Copyright header rewrap** — dart format artifact, fine.

11. CI: pending at review time; no ci_failures.md → not blocking per input. I should mention the PR's own claim (300 network tests green) — but those are VM tests with fakes, which supports finding #1.

12. One more check — `flutter analyze` on web: `dart:html` is deprecated in favor of package:web, but repo convention uses dart:html here already (pre-existing import). Skip.

13. `bind()` timeout timer: `receiver._timeout = Timer(...)` — on timeout the error completes but the blank popup is NOT closed until close() is called by signIn's finally — which happens because callback future completes with error → signIn throws → finally close() → closes popup. Covered.

14. Actually — one more potential real bug: In `openAuthUrlImpl` fallback path after eager navigation threw, `receiver?._popup = null` — but `eager` might still be open and usable-ish; then `_tryOpenPopup(authUrl, ...)` opens a NEW window with name 'fa_oauth' — if the eager window is still alive with that name, the browser navigates THE SAME window again (name match) and returns a handle to it — so `popup` == eager window. Then close() etc. fine. OK not a bug.

15. Line 82: `popup.closed ?? true` — hmm wait, in `close()`: `if (popup != null && _isUsable(popup))` → try close. If popup is a live window → close() → fine.

16. `_originCallback()` — trivial extraction, fine.

Let me also verify the claim "auth_flow_test (5 green)" — 5 tests exist roughly. Fine.

Also double check `sign_in_dialog.dart` catches errors and shows them (so the new AuthFlowException paths surface in UI). Quick grep. Not critical.

One more important verification: the PR description says the eager popup is opened in `bind()` — is `bind()` REALLY called synchronously within the user gesture? Chain: dialog button onPressed → manager.signInWithProvider (async) → NetworkAuthFlow.signIn (async) → `await startReceiver()` → `startOAuthCallbackReceiver()` → `bind()` (async). Each await adds a microtask hop, no macrotask — so window.open runs in the same event-loop task as the click handler → transient activation intact. Verified by reasoning; correct.

But hmm — one caveat: `signInWithProvider` in network_session_manager — does the DIALOG call it directly from onPressed, or after an await (e.g., showing a progress, or `oauthProviders()` fetch)? If the dialog awaits something real (like a network providers fetch or a microtask-only?) — microtasks are fine, network await would kill activation. Let me check showSignInDialog's call path quickly. If it awaits a network call before signInWithProvider, the eager popup in bind would ALREADY be outside the gesture and the whole fix would not work... The PR author claims tested manually (well, claims tests green but those are fakes; manual browser verification implied). Let me check the dialog code to be thorough — this is the make-or-break of the fix.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

playback of sandbox media: `SandboxAudioPlayer` (play/pause, seek slider,
  `m:ss / m:ss`) and `SandboxVideoPlayer` (bounded tap-to-toggle surface,
  progress bar, mute) behind injectable `SandboxAudioController`/
  `SandboxVideoController` abstractions (tests/goldens inject fakes via
  `ChatScreen(audioControllerFactory:/videoControllerFactory:)`, real
  defaults wrap `audioplayers` (`BytesSource` — no file needed) and
  `video_player` (bytes staged to a temp file; web build shows an honest
  "not supported" note). Wired in `chat_screen.dart` for `speak`/
  `generate_music` results plus a `.mp3/.wav/.m4a` (audio) / `.mp4/.mov/
  .webm` (video) extension fallback for any NON-`read`, non-error tool
  result (which is how `generate_video` tiles render); markdown media links open a `showFahMediaDialog` player dialog
  (`onTapLink` — flutter_markdown has no custom link renderer) in the chat
  screen and the Fa chat overlay. Bytes load through the same memoized
  `SandboxImageResolver.load`.
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/chat_message_tile.dart` (shim re-export of
  `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/chat_message_tile.dart`) — the ONE transcript
  message renderer, shared by the chat screen (its `flutter_chat_ui`
  builders delegate) and the in-app Fa chat overlay (`compact: true` for
  tighter panel padding): user/assistant Markdown bubbles (sandbox images
  via `SandboxImageResolver`, selectable), tail-collapsed thinking bubble,
  styled `[ tool ]` tiles with the private collapsible output block,
  `$`-prompt system lines, and inline generated-image/audio/video under
  tool tiles. Never fork message rendering — extend this widget.
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/chat_composer.dart` (ADAPTER over
  `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/chat_composer.dart`) — keeps the app's
  constructor surface (`AgentService` + injectable `uploadPicker`/`asr`/
  `asrTranscriber`/`clipboardImageReader` test fakes) and bridges it to the
  shared composer's hooks: the `UploadPicker` becomes a `FaChatUploadPicker`,
  gallery/camera come from `image_picker`, the ASR stack is wrapped in a
  `FaChatVoiceInput` (transcriber resolved per take via the session's
  media gateway, falling back to the active provider), and the smart-paste
  clipboard image probe rides `pasteboard` (`Pasteboard.image` → PNG bytes;
  native plugin — the desktop/mobile apps need a REBUILD, not a hot reload,
  to register it).
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/app_launcher_screen.dart` — THE app home on
  every layout (`faHomeScreen` in main.dart always returns it; the classic
  sidebar chat home is legacy and `session_sidebar.dart` no longer exists —
  sessions are managed by the chat sheet's pager/menus).
  iOS-home-screen grid of the JS apps (fsRevision-refreshed like
  `AppsGridView`) plus Settings/Files system tiles, laid out on the
  icon-unit geometry (`LauncherGridSpec` in
  `lib/ui/widgets/span_grid_delegate.dart`: 56px icon square + 20px label,
  16px gaps; default 4 columns < 600px, 6 above, clamped 3–8) as a
  `SingleChildScrollView` + `Stack` of `AnimatedPositioned` tiles
  (`packTileSpans`/`layOutTileRects`; issue #166 made the packer
  order-preserving row-wrap: tiles place strictly in list order, a span
  that doesn't fit the remaining row cells wraps to the next row and the
  trailing cells stay blank — no backfilling earlier rows, reading order
  == tile order; spans clamp to the column count), so reorders animate
  live while dragging (center-band hover on an app = folder intent, edge
  halves = insertion preview; drop persists; hold-release without
  movement opens the tile-size menu). Folder tap opens a floating panel
  (rename/dissolve buttons, drag-out-to-ungroup onto the barrier). Tile
  layout persists via
  `LauncherLayoutStore` (`lib/services/launcher_layout_store.dart`,
  `launcher_layout.json` v2: ordered keys `app:<id>`/`system:*`/`folder:<id>`
  + `grid.columns` + `tileSizes` {appId: "WxH"} overrides — agent-editable,
  re-read live on fsRevision; v1 migrates, corrupt file → defaults;
  `syncApps` reconciles with installed apps). Its Stack hosts the
  `SessionChatSheet`.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/session_chat_sheet.dart` — the iMessage-style
  session chat overlay over the launcher, three layers above the app grid:
  the always-visible docked input bar (the shared `ChatComposer` with
  `autofocus: false` — the bar never pops the keyboard at app start;
  leading slot = sessions-drawer toggle with the custom `SessionsGlyph`
  stacked-bubbles icon, turning into the attach button once a session is
  open; trailing = exactly ONE action — the mic while the field is empty
  and idle, stop while streaming-empty, send once text is entered, swapped

## PR Description

## Проблема

Web sign-in из диалога «Sign in with your ai-native.cloud account» был сломан в двух местах:

1. **`Attempting to use a null window in Window.open`** — `NetworkAuthFlow` ждёт сетевой `/initiate` между кликом и `window.open`; к моменту открытия попап теряет transient activation кнопки, браузер блокирует его, а null-backed `WindowBase` падает на любом обращении (в т.ч. на проверке `closed`).
2. **`/oauth/callback` отдавал 404 на GitHub Pages** — статическая receiver-страница из #1048 была удалена коммитом 80a5ebeeb (прямой пуш в main без PR).

## Фикс

- `WebOAuthReceiver.bind()` открывает попап **синхронно в момент клика** (`about:blank`, пока gesture activation жив); `openAuthUrlImpl` лишь навигирует уже открытое окно — навигация существующего окна не требует активации, поэтому `/initiate` RTT между кликом и навигацией безопасен.
- Null-safe `_isUsable` проба (null-backed WindowBase бросает на любом члене), `close()` убирает брошенный попап при провале flow, fallback на прямой open если eager-попап был заблокирован при bind.
- `site/oauth/callback/index.html` восстановлен без изменений (#1048).

Проверено: flutter_app/test/network/* (300 зелёные), auth_flow_test (5 зелёные), анализ чистый. Связано: auth-allowlist fa1.dev — IstiN/learn.ai#69 (уже в проде).

Note: bind() is `async` but nothing awaits before the open — wait, `bind()` is declared `async` and the popup open happens synchronously within the first ticks of the function... In Dart, an `async` function body runs synchronously until the first `await`. There's no `await` before `_tryOpenPopup` — the body executes synchronously up to the `Timer` creation and `return receiver` (which wraps in a future). So the window.open still happens synchronously within the click's task? Let me check: the caller chain — `NetworkSessionManager.signInWithProvider` → `NetworkAuthFlow.signIn` → `await startReceiver()` → `startOAuthCallbackReceiver()` → `bind()`. 

Each `await` in the chain is a microtask boundary, NOT a task boundary. Transient user activation is consumed only by certain APIs (window.open consumes activation? Actually transient activation lasts a few seconds or until consumed by "once-per-activation" APIs like window.open). Microtasks don't yield to the event loop, so the activation is still valid. `oauthInitiate` network await does yield — that's the whole point of the fix; and it happens AFTER bind returns. The awaits between the click handler and window.open are microtask-only (signIn's startReceiver await → microtask; bind has no awaits before open). So the open happens in the same macrotask as the click handler, activation intact. Correct reasoning. 

But wait — `signInWithProvider` is presumably called from a button onPressed handler. Between the click and `NetworkAuthFlow.signIn`, is there any real async gap? Let me check the dialog code that calls signInWithProvider. If there's a network call BEFORE signIn (e.g., fetching providers) — that's not the case; signIn is called directly. OK.

4. **A potential bug: `openAuthUrlImpl` fallback retry uses window name 'fa_oauth' again.** If the eager popup was blocked by the browser, `_popup` is null, we `_tryOpenPopup(authUrl...)`. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

  `m:ss / m:ss`) and `SandboxVideoPlayer` (bounded tap-to-toggle surface,
  progress bar, mute) behind injectable `SandboxAudioController`/
  `SandboxVideoController` abstractions (tests/goldens inject fakes via
  `ChatScreen(audioControllerFactory:/videoControllerFactory:)`, real
  defaults wrap `audioplayers` (`BytesSource` — no file needed) and
  `video_player` (bytes staged to a temp file; web build shows an honest
  "not supported" note). Wired in `chat_screen.dart` for `speak`/
  `generate_music` results plus a `.mp3/.wav/.m4a` (audio) / `.mp4/.mov/
  .webm` (video) extension fallback for any NON-`read`, non-error tool
  result (which is how `generate_video` tiles render); markdown media links open a `showFahMediaDialog` player dialog
  (`onTapLink` — flutter_markdown has no custom link renderer) in the chat
  screen and the Fa chat overlay. Bytes load through the same memoized
  `SandboxImageResolver.load`.
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/chat_message_tile.dart` (shim re-export of
  `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/chat_message_tile.dart`) — the ONE transcript
  message renderer, shared by the chat screen (its `flutter_chat_ui`
  builders delegate) and the in-app Fa chat overlay (`compact: true` for
  tighter panel padding): user/assistant Markdown bubbles (sandbox images
  via `SandboxImageResolver`, selectable), tail-collapsed thinking bubble,
  styled `[ tool ]` tiles with the private collapsible output block,
  `$`-prompt system lines, and inline generated-image/audio/video under
  tool tiles. Never fork message rendering — extend this widget.
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/chat_composer.dart` (ADAPTER over
  `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/chat_composer.dart`) — keeps the app's
  constructor surface (`AgentService` + injectable `uploadPicker`/`asr`/
  `asrTranscriber`/`clipboardImageReader` test fakes) and bridges it to the
  shared composer's hooks: the `UploadPicker` becomes a `FaChatUploadPicker`,
  gallery/camera come from `image_picker`, the ASR stack is wrapped in a
  `FaChatVoiceInput` (transcriber resolved per take via the session's
  media gateway, falling back to the active provider), and the smart-paste
  clipboard image probe rides `pasteboard` (`Pasteboard.image` → PNG bytes;
  native plugin — the desktop/mobile apps need a REBUILD, not a hot reload,
  to register it).
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/app_launcher_screen.dart` — THE app home on
  every layout (`faHomeScreen` in main.dart always returns it; the classic
  sidebar chat home is legacy and `session_sidebar.dart` no longer exists —
  sessions are managed by the chat sheet's pager/menus).
  iOS-home-screen grid of the JS apps (fsRevision-refreshed like
  `AppsGridView`) plus Settings/Files system tiles, laid out on the
  icon-unit geometry (`LauncherGridSpec` in
  `lib/ui/widgets/span_grid_delegate.dart`: 56px icon square + 20px label,
  16px gaps; default 4 columns < 600px, 6 above, clamped 3–8) as a
  `SingleChildScrollView` + `Stack` of `AnimatedPositioned` tiles
  (`packTileSpans`/`layOutTileRects`; issue #166 made the packer
  order-preserving row-wrap: tiles place strictly in list order, a span
  that doesn't fit the remaining row cells wraps to the next row and the
  trailing cells stay blank — no backfilling earlier rows, reading order
  == tile order; spans clamp to the column count), so reorders animate
  live while dragging (center-band hover on an app = folder intent, edge
  halves = insertion preview; drop persists; hold-release without
  movement opens the tile-size menu). Folder tap opens a floating panel
  (rename/dissolve buttons, drag-out-to-ungroup onto the barrier). Tile
  layout persists via
  `LauncherLayoutStore` (`lib/services/launcher_layout_store.dart`,
  `launcher_layout.json` v2: ordered keys `app:<id>`/`system:*`/`folder:<id>`
  + `grid.columns` + `tileSizes` {appId: "WxH"} overrides — agent-editable,
  re-read live on fsRevision; v1 migrates, corrupt file → defaults;
  `syncApps` reconciles with installed apps). Its Stack hosts the
  `SessionChatSheet`.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/session_chat_sheet.dart` — the iMessage-style
  session chat overlay over the launcher, three layers above the app grid:
  the always-visible docked input bar (the shared `ChatComposer` with
  `autofocus: false` — the bar never pops the keyboard at app start;
  leading slot = sessions-drawer toggle with the custom `SessionsGlyph`
  stacked-bubbles icon, turning into the attach button once a session is
  open; trailing = exactly ONE action — the mic while the field is empty
  and idle, stop while streaming-empty, send once text is entered, swapped
  via AnimatedSwitcher scale+fade (the composer's `hideMicWhenNotEmpty`;
  the idle mic sits in the same pill-colored circle the send/stop button
  occupies); the composer carries a stable key so the status-row slot
  toggling never recreates it (that killed the field's focus after send),
  and `_send` restores focus past the IME send action's own unfocus —
  the keyboard stays up for the follow-up message. Focusing the field
  opens the panel right away via
  `onFocusChanged`, `onSent` does too), the sessions drawer sliding in from
  the LEFT (New-session tile + live then persisted sessions rendered with
  the SAME `SessionTile`/`sessionTileSubtitle`/`sessionTileCwdLabel`/
  `showSessionActionsMenu` the wide sidebar exports from
  `sidebar_sessions_list.dart`, persisted open lazily via

  session's OWN on-disk metadata cwd — a live session's env reports the

- **Title**: fix(web): restore /oauth/callback page + eager OAuth popup (web sign-in end-to-end)
- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **Deletions**: -22

## PR Description

## Проблема

Web sign-in из диалога «Sign in with your ai-native.cloud account» был сломан в двух местах:

1. **`Attempting to use a null window in Window.open`** — `NetworkAuthFlow` ждёт сетевой `/initiate` между кликом и `window.open`; к моменту открытия попап теряет transient activation кнопки, браузер блокирует его, а null-backed `WindowBase` падает на любом обращении (в т.ч. на проверке `closed`).
2. **`/oauth/callback` отдавал 404 на GitHub Pages** — статическая receiver-страница из #1048 была удалена коммитом 80a5ebeeb (прямой пуш в main без PR).

## Фикс

- `WebOAuthReceiver.bind()` открывает попап **синхронно в момент клика** (`about:blank`, пока gesture activation жив); `openAuthUrlImpl` лишь навигирует уже открытое окно — навигация существующего окна не требует активации, поэтому `/initiate` RTT между кликом и навигацией безопасен.
- Null-safe `_isUsable` проба (null-backed WindowBase бросает на любом члене), `close()` убирает брошенный попап при провале flow, fallback на прямой open если eager-попап был заблокирован при bind.
- `site/oauth/callback/index.html` восстановлен без изменений (#1048).

Проверено: flutter_app/test/network/* (300 зелёные), auth_flow_test (5 зелёные), анализ чистый. Связано: auth-allowlist fa1.dev — IstiN/learn.ai#69 (уже в проде).

Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8.   `m:ss / m:ss`) and `SandboxVideoPlayer` (bounded tap-to-toggle surface,
  progress bar, mute) behind injectable `SandboxAudioController`/
  `SandboxVideoController` abstractions (tests/goldens inject fakes via
  `ChatScreen(audioControllerFactory:/videoControllerFactory:)`, real
  defaults wrap `audioplayers` (`BytesSource` — no file needed) and
  `video_player` (bytes staged to a temp file; web build shows an honest
  "not supported" note). Wired in `chat_screen.dart` for `speak`/
  `generate_music` results plus a `.mp3/.wav/.m4a` (audio) / `.mp4/.mov/
  .webm` (video) extension fallback for any NON-`read`, non-error tool
  result (which is how `generate_video` tiles render); markdown media links open a `showFahMediaDialog` player dialog
  (`onTapLink` — flutter_markdown has no custom link renderer) in the chat
  screen and the Fa chat overlay. Bytes load through the same memoized
  `SandboxImageResolver.load`.
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/chat_message_tile.dart` (shim re-export of
  `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/chat_message_tile.dart`) — the ONE transcript
  message renderer, shared by the chat screen (its `flutter_chat_ui`
  builders delegate) and the in-app Fa chat overlay (`compact: true` for
  tighter panel padding): user/assistant Markdown bubbles (sandbox images
  via `SandboxImageResolver`, selectable), tail-collapsed thinking bubble,
  styled `[ tool ]` tiles with the private collapsible output block,
  `$`-prompt system lines, and inline generated-image/audio/video under
  tool tiles. Never fork message rendering — extend this widget.
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/widgets/chat_composer.dart` (ADAPTER over
  `packages/fa_ui/lib/src/chat/chat_composer.dart`) — keeps the app's
  constructor surface (`AgentService` + injectable `uploadPicker`/`asr`/
  `asrTranscriber`/`clipboardImageReader` test fakes) and bridges it to the
  shared composer's hooks: the `UploadPicker` becomes a `FaChatUploadPicker`,
  gallery/camera come from `image_picker`, the ASR stack is wrapped in a
  `FaChatVoiceInput` (transcriber resolved per take via the session's
  media gateway, falling back to the active provider), and the smart-paste
  clipboard image probe rides `pasteboard` (`Pasteboard.image` → PNG bytes;
  native plugin — the desktop/mobile apps need a REBUILD, not a hot reload,
  to register it).
- `flutter_app/lib/ui/screens/app_launcher_screen.dart` — THE app home on
  every layout (`faHomeScreen` in main.dart always returns it; the classic
  sidebar chat home is legacy and `session_sidebar.dart` no longer exists —
  sessions are managed by the chat sheet's pager/menus).
  iOS-home-screen grid of the JS apps (fsRevision-refreshed like
  `AppsGridView`) plus Settings/Files system tiles, laid out on the
  icon-unit geometry (`LauncherGridSpec` in
  `lib/ui/widgets/span_grid_delegate.dart`: 56px icon square + 20px label,
  16px gaps; default 4 columns < 600px, 6 above, clamped 3–8) as a
  `SingleChildScrollView` + `Stack` of `AnimatedPositioned` tiles
  (`packTileSpans`/`layOutTileRects`; issue #166 made the packer
  order-preserving row-wrap: tiles place strictly in list order, a span
  that doesn't fit the remaining row cells wraps to the next row and the
  trailing cells stay blank — no backfilling earlier rows, reading order
  == tile order; spans clamp to the column count), so reorders animate
  live while dragging (center-band hover on an app = folder intent, edge
  halves = insertion preview; drop persists; hold-release without
  movement opens the tile-size menu). Folder tap opens a floating panel
  (rename/dissolve buttons, drag-out-to-ungroup onto the barrier). Tile
  layout persists via
  `LauncherLayoutStore` (`lib/services/launcher_layout_store.dart`,
  `launcher_layout.json` v2: ordered keys `app:<id>`/`system:*`/`folder:<id>`
  + `grid.columns` + `tileSizes` {appId: "WxH"} overrides — agent-editable,
  re-read live on fsRevision; v1 migrates, corrupt file → defaults;
  `syncApps` reconciles with installed apps). Its Stack hosts the
  `SessionChatSheet`.
- `flutter_app/lib/apps/session_chat_sheet.dart` — the iMessage-style
  session chat overlay over the launcher, three layers above the app grid:
  the always-visible docked input bar (the shared `ChatComposer` with
  `autofocus: false` — the bar never pops the keyboard at app start;
  leading slot = sessions-drawer toggle with the custom `SessionsGlyph`
  stacked-bubbles icon, turning into the attach button once a session is
  open; trailing = exactly ONE action — the mic while the field is empty
  and idle, stop while streaming-empty, send once text is entered, swapped
  via AnimatedSwitcher scale+fade (the composer's `hideMicWhenNotEmpty`;
  the idle mic sits in the same pill-colored circle the send/stop button
  occupies); the composer carries a stable key so the status-row slot
  toggling never recreates it (that killed the field's focus after send),
  and `_send` restores focus past the IME send action's own unfocus —
  the keyboard stays up for the follow-up message. Focusing the field
  opens the panel right away via
  `onFocusChanged`, `onSent` does too), the sessions drawer sliding in from
  the LEFT (New-session tile + live then persisted sessions rendered with
  the SAME `SessionTile`/`sessionTileSubtitle`/`sessionTileCwdLabel`/
  `showSessionActionsMenu` the wide sidebar exports from
  `sidebar_sessions_list.dart`, persisted open lazily via

## PR Description

## Проблема

Web sign-in из диалога «Sign in with your ai-native.cloud account» был сломан в двух местах:

1. **`Attempting to use a null window in Window.open`** — `NetworkAuthFlow` ждёт сетевой `/initiate` между кликом и `window.open`; к моменту открытия попап теряет transient activation кнопки, браузер блокирует его, а null-backed `WindowBase` падает на любом обращении (в т.ч. на проверке `closed`).
2. **`/oauth/callback` отдавал 404 на GitHub Pages** — статическая receiver-страница из #1048 была удалена коммитом 80a5ebeeb (прямой пуш в main без PR).

## Фикс

- `WebOAuthReceiver.bind()` открывает попап **синхронно в момент клика** (`about:blank`, пока gesture activation жив); `openAuthUrlImpl` лишь навигирует уже открытое окно — навигация существующего окна не требует активации, поэтому `/initiate` RTT между кликом и навигацией безопасен.
- Null-safe `_isUsable` проба (null-backed WindowBase бросает на любом члене), `close()` убирает брошенный попап при провале flow, fallback на прямой open если eager-попап был заблокирован при bind.
- `site/oauth/callback/index.html` восстановлен без изменений (#1048).

Проверено: flutter_app/test/network/* (300 зелёные), auth_flow_test (5 зелёные), анализ чистый. Связано: auth-allowlist fa1.dev — IstiN/learn.ai#69 (уже в проде).

arguments.content:
# 🚨 IMPORTANT: The rewritten web receiver has zero automated coverage

`WebOAuthReceiver` (this file) is the core of the PR — eager popup open, null-safe
usability probing, navigation fallback, stray-popup cleanup — yet none of it is
exercised by any test. `auth_loopback.dart`'s conditional import selects the
**io/stub** variants under VM tests, so the "flutter_app/test/network/* (300 green)"
claim from the PR description runs entirely against `FakeOAuthReceiver`
(`test/network/fakes.dart`); `WebOAuthReceiver` compiles only under `dart:html`
and no `-p chrome` test leg exists for `flutter_app` in CI.

This matters here more than usual:

- The bug this PR fixes (null-window crash) and the 404 regression it restores
  (#1048's page deleted by a direct push to main) are both examples of web-only
  glue silently rotting — exactly the code that needs a pinned test, not manual
  verification.
- The repo's quality gates ratchet **changed-line coverage** (`scripts/diff_coverage.py`
  in the `coverage-gate` leg); ~112 changed lines in this file are structurally
  uncoverable on the VM, so the leg may flag this PR once CI concludes (checks were
  still pending at review time).

Suggested follow-up (not necessarily this PR):

1. Add a `flutter test --platform chrome` scaffold for `test/network/` and pin at
   least the sequencing: `bind()` opens a usable popup, `openAuthUrlImpl` navigates
   it and starts the poll, `close()` closes the window and clears `_active`, blocked
   popup → `AuthFlowException`.
2. Or extract the popup state machine (open/navigate/probe/close decisions) into a
   pure injectable unit testable on the VM, keeping only the `dart:html` calls
   behind a tiny seam.

💡 **SUGGESTION: overlapping sign-ins share one window name and can close each other's popup**

`bind()` overwrites `_active` unconditionally and every open reuses the window name
`'fa_oauth'` (line 70). Per the spec, `window.open(url, 'fa_oauth')` when a window
with that name already exists **navigates the existing browsing context** instead of
opening a new one. So if two flows ever overlap:

1. Flow A is bound, its eager `about:blank` popup lingers through the whole
   `/initiate` round-trip (this PR widens that window — before the PR the popup only
   existed after `openAuthUrl`).
2. Flow B binds → its "new" popup *is* A's window (name match).
3. A finishes/fails → A's `finally close()` closes the window B is driving, or A's
   poll reports it closed → both flows fail confusingly.

Today the sign-in dialog serializes providers through one busy slot, so the overlap
is only reachable from future callers of `NetworkSessionManager.signInWithProvider`.
Cheap hardening: in `bind()`, call `_active?.close()` (or at least close its popup)
before rebinding, or note the invariant in the `_active` doc. Pre-existing naming,
so not blocking — but the eager open makes the hazard easier to hit.

## PR Description

## Проблема

Web sign-in из диалога «Sign in with your ai-native.cloud account» был сломан в двух местах:

1. **`Attempting to use a null window in Window.open`** — `NetworkAuthFlow` ждёт сетевой `/initiate` между кликом и `window.open`; к моменту открытия попап теряет transient activation кнопки, браузер блокирует его, а null-backed `WindowBase` падает на любом обращении (в т.ч. на проверке `closed`).
2. **`/oauth/callback` отдавал 404 на GitHub Pages** — статическая receiver-страница из #1048 была удалена коммитом 80a5ebeeb (прямой пуш в main без PR).

## Фикс

- `WebOAuthReceiver.bind()` открывает попап **синхронно в момент клика** (`about:blank`, пока gesture activation жив); `openAuthUrlImpl` лишь навигирует уже открытое окно — навигация существующего окна не требует активации, поэтому `/initiate` RTT между кликом и навигацией безопасен.
- Null-safe `_isUsable` проба (null-backed WindowBase бросает на любом члене), `close()` убирает брошенный попап при провале flow, fallback на прямой open если eager-попап был заблокирован при bind.
- `site/oauth/callback/index.html` восстановлен без изменений (#1048).

Проверено: flutter_app/test/network/* (300 зелёные), auth_flow_test (5 зелёные), анализ чистый. Связано: auth-allowlist fa1.dev — IstiN/learn.ai#69 (уже в проде).

In Dart, an `async` function body runs synchronously until the first `await`. There's no `await` before `_tryOpenPopup` — the body executes synchronously up to the `Timer` creation and `return receiver` (which wraps in a future). So the window.open still happens synchronously within the click's task? Let me check: the caller chain — `NetworkSessionManager.signInWithProvider` → `NetworkAuthFlow.signIn` → `await startReceiver()` → `startOAuthCallbackReceiver()` → `bind()`. 

Each `await` in the chain is a microtask boundary, NOT a task boundary. Transient user activation is consumed only by certain APIs (window.open consumes activation? Actually transient activation lasts a few seconds or until consumed by "once-per-activation" APIs like window.open). Microtasks don't yield to the event loop, so the activation is still valid. `oauthInitiate` network await does yield — that's the whole point of the fix; and it happens AFTER bind returns. The awaits between the click handler and window.open are microtask-only (signIn's startReceiver await → microtask; bind has no awaits before open). {"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: overlapping sign-ins share one window name and can close each other's popup**

`bind()` overwrites `_active` unconditionally and every open reuses the window name
`'fa_oauth'` (line 70). Per the spec, `window.open(url, 'fa_oauth')` when a window
with that name already exists **navigates the existing browsing context** instead of
opening a new one. So if two flows ever overlap:

1. Flow A is bound, its eager `about:blank` popup lingers through the whole
   `/initiate` round-trip (this PR widens that window — before the PR the popup only
   existed after `openAuthUrl`).
2. Flow B binds → its "new" popup *is* A's window (name match).
3. A finishes/fails → A's `finally close()` closes the window B is driving, or A's
   poll reports it closed → both flows fail confusingly.

Today the sign-in dialog serializes providers through one busy slot, so the overlap
is only reachable from future callers of `NetworkSessionManager.signInWithProvider`.
Cheap hardening: in `bind()`, call `_active?.close()` (or at least close its popup)
before rebinding, or note the invariant in the `_active` doc. Pre-existing naming,
so not blocking — but the eager open makes the hazard easier to hit.

💡 **SUGGESTION: misleading error when the user closes the eager blank popup themselves**

While `/initiate` is in flight, the user stares at a featureless `about:blank`
window — closing it is a natural reaction. The close is not observed anywhere:

the direct-open fallback here, which after the `/initiate` await usually finds the
transient activation expired, gets blocked, and surfaces:

> "the sign-in popup was blocked by the browser"

…when the user actually closed the window themselves (the accurate message —
"the sign-in window was closed" — is what the poll would have reported had it been
running).

Options: start the 300 ms poll in `bind()` (it is a no-op on a same-origin blank
URL — no `code`/`error` params), or in the fallback path distinguish
"eager popup was closed by the user" from "open was blocked" and pick the message
accordingly. Purely a message-accuracy nit; the failure itself is handled honestly.

## PR Description

## Проблема

Web sign-in из диалога «Sign in with your ai-native.cloud account» был сломан в двух местах:

1. **`Attempting to use a null window in Window.open`** — `NetworkAuthFlow` ждёт сетевой `/initiate` между кликом и `window.open`; к моменту открытия попап теряет transient activation кнопки, браузер блокирует его, а null-backed `WindowBase` падает на любом обращении (в т.ч. на проверке `closed`).
2. **`/oauth/callback` отдавал 404 на GitHub Pages** — статическая receiver-страница из #1048 была удалена коммитом 80a5ebeeb (прямой пуш в main без PR).

## Фикс

- `WebOAuthReceiver.bind()` открывает попап **синхронно в момент клика** (`about:blank`, пока gesture activation жив); `openAuthUrlImpl` лишь навигирует уже открытое окно — навигация существующего окна не требует активации, поэтому `/initiate` RTT между кликом и навигацией безопасен.
- Null-safe `_isUsable` проба (null-backed WindowBase бросает на любом члене), `close()` убирает брошенный попап при провале flow, fallback на прямой open если eager-попап был заблокирован при bind.
- `site/oauth/callback/index.html` восстановлен без изменений (#1048).

Microtasks don't yield to the event loop, so the activation is still valid. `oauthInitiate` network await does yield — that's the whole point of the fix; and it happens AFTER bind returns. {"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: overlapping sign-ins share one window name and can close each other's popup**

`bind()` overwrites `_active` unconditionally and every open reuses the window name
`'fa_oauth'` (line 70). Per the spec, `window.open(url, 'fa_oauth')` when a window
with that name already exists **navigates the existing browsing context** instead of
opening a new one. So if two flows ever overlap:

1. Flow A is bound, its eager `about:blank` popup lingers through the whole
   `/initiate` round-trip (this PR widens that window — before the PR the popup only
   existed after `openAuthUrl`).
2. Flow B binds → its "new" popup *is* A's window (name match).
3. A finishes/fails → A's `finally close()` closes the window B is driving, or A's
   poll reports it closed → both flows fail confusingly.

Today the sign-in dialog serializes providers through one busy slot, so the overlap
is only reachable from future callers of `NetworkSessionManager.signInWithProvider`.
Cheap hardening: in `bind()`, call `_active?.close()` (or at least close its popup)
before rebinding, or note the invariant in the `_active` doc. Pre-existing naming,
so not blocking — but the eager open makes the hazard easier to hit.

## PR Description

## Проблема

Web sign-in из диалога «Sign in with your ai-native.cloud account» был сломан в двух местах:

1. **`Attempting to use a null window in Window.open`** — `NetworkAuthFlow` ждёт сетевой `/initiate` между кликом и `window.open`; к моменту открытия попап теряет transient activation кнопки, браузер блокирует его, а null-backed `WindowBase` падает на любом обращении (в т.ч. на проверке `closed`).
2. **`/oauth/callback` отдавал 404 на GitHub Pages** — статическая receiver-страница из #1048 была удалена коммитом 80a5ebeeb (прямой пуш в main без PR).

## Фикс

- `WebOAuthReceiver.bind()` открывает попап **синхронно в момент клика** (`about:blank`, пока gesture activation жив); `openAuthUrlImpl` лишь навигирует уже открытое окно — навигация существующего окна не требует активации, поэтому `/initiate` RTT между кликом и навигацией безопасен.
- Null-safe `_isUsable` проба (null-backed WindowBase бросает на любом члене), `close()` убирает брошенный попап при провале flow, fallback на прямой open если eager-попап был заблокирован при bind.
- `site/oauth/callback/index.html` восстановлен без изменений (#1048).

In Dart, an `async` function body runs synchronously until the first `await`. There's no `await` before `_tryOpenPopup` — the body executes synchronously up to the `Timer` creation and `return receiver` (which wraps in a future). Let me check: the caller chain — `NetworkSessionManager.signInWithProvider` → `NetworkAuthFlow.signIn` → `await startReceiver()` → `startOAuthCallbackReceiver()` → `bind()`. 

Each `await` in the chain is a microtask boundary, NOT a task boundary. Transient user activation is consumed only by certain APIs (window.open consumes activation? Actually transient activation lasts a few seconds or until consumed by "once-per-activation" APIs like window.open). Microtasks don't yield to the event loop, so the activation is still valid. `oauthInitiate` network await does yield — that's the whole point of the fix; and it happens AFTER bind returns. The awaits between the click handler and window.open are microtask-only (signIn's startReceiver await → microtask; bind has no awaits before open). So the open happens in the same macrotask as the click handler, activation intact. Correct reasoning. 

But wait — `signInWithProvider` is presumably called from a button onPressed handler. Between the click and `NetworkAuthFlow.signIn`, is there any real async gap? Let me check the dialog code that calls signInWithProvider. If there's a network call BEFORE signIn (e.g., fetching providers) — that's not the case; signIn is called directly. OK.

4. **A potential bug: `openAuthUrlImpl` fallback retry uses window name 'fa_oauth' again.** If the eager popup was blocked by the browser, `_popup` is null, we `_tryOpenPopup(authUrl...)`. This happens after the initiate await — activation likely expired → blocked → null → throw AuthFlowException. Honest. OK.

5. **What if the user closes the eager about:blank popup while initiate is in-flight?** Then in openAuthUrlImpl, `_isUsable(eager)` → false → fallback direct open attempt. `window.open` with name 'fa_oauth' — the window with that name is CLOSED, so a new window opens... but activation expired → blocked → null → "popup was blocked" error. Hmm, this is a real UX regression path vs the old code? In the old code, the same thing would happen (open after await → blocked). So no regression; same failure. Fine.

6. **`close()` when `_active == this` check** — added guard so an older receiver isn't cleared when a newer bind happened. Wait, actually there's still an issue: `bind()` unconditionally overwrites `_active = receiver` WITHOUT closing the previous receiver's eager popup. If a previous flow is still live (user opened sign-in A, then somehow triggers sign-in B — e.g., two dialogs, or a re-click after a flow that never completes), bind B replaces `_active`, and A's `finally close()` correctly cleans A (close checks `_active == this` before clearing, and closes `_popup`). So A's popup is closed by A's close(). Fine — no leak.

But hold on: both popups share the window name 'fa_oauth'. A's popup named 'fa_oauth' is open; bind B's `_tryOpenPopup('about:blank', ...)` with the same name would NAVIGATE/reuse A's window instead of opening a second window (window.open with an existing name targets the existing browsing context). Then A's flow closes A's popup (which is now B's window!) — actually A.close() closes `_popup` which is the SAME window B is using. So B's flow silently loses its popup. {"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: overlapping sign-ins share one window name and can close each other's popup**

`bind()` overwrites `_active` unconditionally and every open reuses the window name
`'fa_oauth'` (line 70). Per the spec, `window.open(url, 'fa_oauth')` when a window
with that name already exists **navigates the existing browsing context** instead of
opening a new one. So if two flows ever overlap:

1. Flow A is bound, its eager `about:blank` popup lingers through the whole
   `/initiate` round-trip (this PR widens that window — before the PR the popup only
   existed after `openAuthUrl`).
2. Flow B binds → its "new" popup *is* A's window (name match).
3. A finishes/fails → A's `finally close()` closes the window B is driving, or A's
   poll reports it closed → both flows fail confusingly.

Today the sign-in dialog serializes providers through one busy slot, so the overlap
is only reachable from future callers of `NetworkSessionManager.signInWithProvider`.
Cheap hardening: in `bind()`, call `_active?.close()` (or at least close its popup)
before rebinding, or note the invariant in the `_active` doc. Pre-existing naming,
so not blocking — but the eager open makes the hazard easier to hit.
